voice: Arena TTS (en, narration) — chosen by owner audition 2026-10-14
intent: Wonder first, then quiet unease: the audience should feel the strangeness of the sky running a wire, admire the people who improvised, and leave thinking about now — without fear-mongering.
pacing_profile: intrigued hush on the hook, calm scene-setting, a breathless sprint (v03) and a peak list (v06), a warm human beat (v05), reflective slow-down for Carrington's caution (v08), then a held breath on the near miss and a reverent close
pause_policy: Ellipses are real held breaths (the hook, the storm, the batteries, the near miss); longer silences once the story turns reflective (v08–v10), and the longest hold at the end. Never pause mid-phrase except at marked ellipses.

lines.text: In 1859, two telegraph operators unplugged their batteries… and kept on talking. The power was coming from the sky.
lines.direction: Intimate and intrigued, like sharing a secret that sounds impossible. Let the ellipsis hang; a small lift on 'kept on talking'; 'from the sky' lands low and certain.

lines.text: On September 1st, at 11:18 in the morning, the astronomer Richard Carrington was sketching sunspots… when two patches of intensely bright, white light broke out.
lines.direction: Calm storyteller setting the scene; unhurried on the date and time. Slight wonder rising on 'intensely bright, white light'.

lines.text: He ran to find a witness. Within sixty seconds, it was fading. Five minutes, and it was gone.
lines.direction: Quick, breathless sentences; the hurry of a man running. Drop the energy on 'it was gone', almost deflated.

lines.text: About seventeen hours later, Earth's magnetic field began to shake… and the night sky turned blood red, as far south as Cuba.
lines.direction: Building dread. Weight on 'seventeen hours'; hold the ellipsis; 'blood red' slow and vivid.

lines.text: In the Rocky Mountains, campers woke after midnight, and some started making breakfast. They thought it was dawn.
lines.direction: A touch of warmth and gentle amusement; the human, almost funny detail. 'They thought it was dawn' soft and slightly awed.

lines.text: Telegraph lines went wild. Sparks jumped from the equipment, operators took shocks, and telegraph paper caught fire.
lines.direction: Peak energy: a rapid list, each clause hitting harder. 'Caught fire' crisp, then stop.

lines.text: So between Boston and Portland, the operators disconnected their batteries… and worked the line for about two hours, on the aurora's current alone.
lines.direction: Admiring, steady: ingenuity under pressure. Let the ellipsis breathe; quiet pride on 'on the aurora's current alone'.

lines.text: Carrington had seen the flare, and the storm. But he wouldn't claim they were connected. One swallow, he said, does not make a summer.
lines.direction: Reflective and respectful of his caution. Slow down for the quote; small pauses around 'he said'.

lines.text: In July 2012, a storm at least as strong crossed Earth's orbit. One week earlier… and it would have hit us.
lines.direction: Modern, close, unsettling. Plain delivery of the date; a long held breath at the ellipsis; 'hit us' quiet, not dramatic.

lines.text: In 1859, the sky ran a telegraph line. Next time… it will find a world built on wires.
lines.direction: Slow, warm and grave: the closing thought. Leave real space after 'telegraph line'; the last words almost whispered.
